sentences.text: Triceratops possessed a large bony frill, three horns on its skull, and a massive four-legged body.
This herbivore measured approximately 8 to 9 meters in length and weighed up to 6 to 10 metric tons.
A specific specimen named Kelsey measured 22 to 24 feet long, had a 6.5-foot skull, stood 7.5 feet tall, and was estimated to weigh 5.4 metric tons.
The genus Triceratops was first described in 1889 by the American paleontologist Othniel Charles Marsh.
The first named fossil specimen attributed to Triceratops was found by George Lyman Cannon near Denver, Colorado, in the spring of 1887.
Othniel Charles Marsh ordered John Bell Hatcher to locate and salvage the skull that became the holotype, which was collected in 1888 from the Lance Formation of Wyoming.

While Triceratops was certainly quadrupedal, its posture is debated; originally believed to have sprawling front legs, evidence now suggests an upright stance with elbows flexed behind, similar to a modern rhinoceros.
Triceratops likely coexisted with and was preyed upon by Tyrannosaurus rex.
Remains of Triceratops show signs of predation or scavenging by Tyrannosaurus, particularly on the largest specimen, with breakage and puncture wounds on the front limb bones.
In 2012, a group of three Triceratops of varying sizes from adult to juvenile were found near Newcastle, Wyoming.
Triceratops is classified as a genus of chasmosaurine ceratopsian dinosaur.
Two species, T. horridus and T. prorsus, are currently considered valid.
T. horridus is the type species of the genus Triceratops, originally named Ceratops horridus by Marsh in 1889.
T. prorsus was named by Marsh in 1890.
Triceratops lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
It lived between 69 and 66 million years ago during the late Maastrichtian age.
Triceratops lived on the island continent of Laramidia, which is now part of western North America.
A 2010 study suggested that Torosaurus represents the mature form of Triceratops, a view that has been highly disputed.
Recent interpretations suggest that Triceratops' frills and horns were primarily used for species identification, courtship, and dominance displays rather than just defense.
Some researchers argue that variations in Triceratops skulls represent a single species with sexual dimorphism rather than multiple species.
Footprints named Ceratopsipes goldenensis found in the Upper Cretaceous Laramie Formation of Colorado may have been made by Triceratops or the related Torosaurus.
Researchers suggest it is unlikely that the nipple-like projections on Triceratops feature scales bore bristles like those found in other ceratopsians.
